# DSH Team Bots
中文
`dsh-team-bots` is a DSH plugin that turns one workspace into a team: project group chats, a task bo
ard, write-scope parallel scheduling, shared memory and skills, approval cards, usage and cost, and
a personal WeChat channel. Every run keeps its trajectory, duration, token count and cost.
## Requirements

- Node.js ≥ 22.19
- the DSH CLI (`dsh`)
The plugin runs inside the DSH Web process. It has no standalone service and no port of its own.

## Open the workspace
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The first visit exchanges the current startup token for a 30-day login cookie. Auto-login means anyo
ne who can reach the port becomes owner, so listen on the local machine or a trusted network; for pu
blic use put an HTTPS reverse proxy in front that forwards Host and WebSocket correctly.
## What the workspace does
### Group chats and dispatch
Every project is a group chat. A bot can also be addressed one-to-one in a dispatch view. All traffi
c for one bot — task dispatch, group chat, direct message, one-to-one chat — lands on a single contr
ol-plane session, and that bot runs one task at a time; different bots still run in parallel.
### Task board
States: backlog, todo, in progress, blocked, in review, done, canceled. A card carries assignee, pri
ority, parent/child links, tags, write scopes, an optional time budget (a hard limit that aborts the
run), comments, and its own usage. Rows are grouped by state and can be dragged onto another group
and its own usage. Rows are grouped by state and can be dragged onto another group to change status.
### Write scopes and parallel scheduling
A card declares the paths it will write, relative to the project working directory. Two runs of the
same project run in parallel only when both declare scopes and the path prefixes do not overlap; a c
ard with no declared scope is treated as serial. An urgent card may be exempted from the queue — the
exemption is written into the card's creation message rather than applied silently.
### Memory, skills, evolution proposals
Memory entries are written, reviewed, frozen and archived by the owner, and are readable by every bo
t in the project. Skills come from a shared skill root plus per-project skills; changing them goes t
hrough a proposal, an approval and an apply, with a canary stage before promotion to full effect. Th
e same path can change a bot's role instructions.
### Approval and question cards
When a bot asks for a tool approval, a secret, or an answer, the workspace shows a card in the chat.
The owner approves, denies or answers in place, and the decision is recorded on the card.
### Usage and cost
The usage page breaks the numbers down by model, bot and project, exports CSV, and reads model price
s from configuration.
### Workspace settings
Run limits (timeout abort, no-progress watchdog, review idle threshold), budgets and retention windo
ws are set per workspace, together with the interface preferences and the local DSH paths.
### Terminal, channels, secrets
A per-project terminal runs commands in the project directory. The WeChat channel binds by QR code a
nd pushes task activity to the owner's WeChat. Secrets are scoped to the team or to one project; val
ues are only ever shown as a fingerprint and are handed out as one-time runtime copies that expire.
## Configuration
| Variable | Default | Meaning |

| `DSH_TEAM_WORKSPACE` | `~/.dsh/workspace/team-bots` | team workspace root |
| `DSH_TEAM_DATA` | `<
workspace>/.data` | database and run records |
Every other variable, its default, and its resolution order (explicit env > value saved in the works
pace > code default) live in `src/config.ts`; `.env.example` lists the common ones. Do not put a `.e
nv` file in the repository root — it would leak `DSH_*` into `npm test` and `npm run dev`.
`DSH_TEAM_DATA` holds `team.sqlite`, `wechat-channel.sqlite`, `secret.key`, `memory/`, `messages/` a
nd `secrets-runtime/`. Back up `secret.key` together with the data: without it the stored ciphertext
cannot be decrypted.

## Release
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The tool pushes `dev`, lands it on `main` (fast-forward when possible, otherwise a content snapshot)
, pushes `main` and the tag, then syncs `dev` back. Publishing uses npm OIDC trusted publishing — no
`NPM_TOKEN` — and the workflow installs npm ≥ 11.5.1 before publishing.
